outcomes: A CI job adds --upload to putnami observe and its change evidence document reaches the reporter it selected, Putnami Cloud by default
A CI job that uploads gets the URL of the full report its reporter answered, in the log and on the pull or merge request note
A third party writes its own reporter as an extension that answers one subcommand, with no change to observe or to the CLI
An upload that fails leaves a diagnostic in the log and never fails the CI job
nonGoals: Talking to Putnami Cloud: the reporter owns the routes, the token and the retries
Uploading a document that does not validate against protocol/evidence v1
Choosing the reporter from the workspace configuration: a CI job outside a workspace has none

requirements.text: With --upload, putnami observe writes the evidence document to the --evidence path, else to a temporary file it removes, then runs the CLI that started it, or putnami on PATH, as <name> evidence-report --file <path> --output=json, where <name> is the name without scope of the extension PUTNAMI_EVIDENCE_REPORTER selects, @putnami/cloud when the variable is unset. The reporter's standard error goes to observe's standard error.

Observe reads the reporter's standard output as one protocol CLI version 2 result, and copies any other output to its standard error, so --output=json still prints one document. When the upload succeeded and data.reportUrl is an absolute https URL without credentials, observe prints it on standard error and the summary note links it. A reporter that answers no result or no such URL still uploaded, with no diagnostic. A failure result adds its error message to observe.upload_failed.

A selector that is not an extension name, a document that was not written, a reporter that cannot start, exits non-zero or runs past two minutes each give one warning diagnostic, observe.upload_failed, and putnami observe still exits 0.
